h1: Microbrewery capital costs: where the money goes
title: Microbrewery Capital Costs | Craft Beer School
desc: A map of the capital cost of a microbrewery: equipment, building work, utilities, licences, pre-opening costs and the contingency owners forget.
teaser: The brewhouse is the part everyone prices. The building, the utilities and the opening months are where budgets break.
standfirst: Capital cost is more than the price of a brewhouse. This guide lists every block of spending, explains why each is easy to under-count and shows how to build a budget you can defend.
sections: Start with the blocks, not a total

Ask a supplier what a microbrewery costs and you will hear the price of a brewhouse. The real project cost is that number plus a long list of others. We split capital cost into blocks so nothing is missed: brewing equipment, cold side and packaging, utilities and services, building and fit-out, licences and professional fees, pre-opening costs and working capital.

This guide gives no prices. Quotes change with exchange rates, specification and supplier. Any figure we printed would age quickly. What we can give you is the structure and the questions.
Brewing equipment and the cold side

The brewhouse (mash tun, kettle, whirlpool), fermenters, a bright tank, a glycol chiller and the piping and valves between them make up the core. Check what is included in each quote: control panel, pumps, hoses, a CIP set and the cold room. Two quotes that look 20 per cent apart often cover different scope.

Cooling is where hot climates bite. A glycol system sized for a cool country may struggle in an Indian summer, so ask the supplier to size the chiller for your ambient temperature, not a catalogue default.

Draught-only is the cheapest way to start. Kegs and a keg washer and filler add a modest amount. A canning or bottling line costs far more. A mobile contract canner is an alternative to owning one. Decide the channel first, then the equipment. Our guide on the unit economics of a keg, a can and a pint shows why.

Brewing needs steam or electric heating, cold and hot water, drainage for wastewater, compressed air for some equipment, CO2 storage and reliable power. Each has a cost to install. Some need approvals. Water quality may need treatment. Effluent may need a treatment step before it leaves the site. Pollution control and fire approvals vary by state, so ask early.

Power cuts matter. A fermenter at temperature can survive a few hours, but a chiller that stops in July does not give you much time.

A brewery needs a floor that drains and can be cleaned, with a fall to the drains, walls that can be washed, enough ceiling height for the tanks and a way to get them in through the door. Many projects discover that the landlord's building cannot take tank weight or that a tank will not pass the doorway. Check this before you sign a lease. For a brewpub add the kitchen, the dining room and toilets. The cost of all that often exceeds the brewing equipment.
Licences, fees and the opening months

Licensing in India is state by state. The process, the timings and the fees change. Budget a line for licences, approvals and an adviser. Confirm the amounts with the authority. The same applies in any country: check with the regulator.

Plan for the equipment's installation and commissioning as well. A brewhouse arrives, but it needs trained hands, a first cleaning and water tests before a saleable brew comes out. Then comes the period before the first sale. You will pay rent, salaries and utilities while you commission, brew test batches and wait for approvals. The pre-revenue period can run to several months. A licence delay can extend it, so keep a note of which approvals gate which spending. This cash belongs in the project cost.
Contingency and how to present it

Check the exchange rate on every imported item, because a brewhouse priced in euros and paid in rupees moves with the currency between quote and payment. Duty and freight on imported equipment belong in the budget too. Add a contingency to the whole budget. Owners commonly choose a percentage, but the right level depends on how firm your quotes are and how far along the building is. Put it in as a visible line. A lender or investor who sees no contingency assumes you have not thought about it.

If you need to present the numbers to a bank or investor, a structured project report puts these blocks, the means of finance and the repayment plan on one page. See what the bank looks at.
faqs: What is the biggest cost in a microbrewery?
It varies. In a production brewery it is usually the brewing and packaging equipment. In a brewpub the building, kitchen and fit-out can match or exceed it.
Should I buy new or second-hand equipment?
Second-hand can save money but carries risk in condition, parts and documentation. Inspect it and get a written specification either way.
Do I need to budget for the months before opening?
Yes. Rent, salaries and utilities run while you wait for approvals and brew test batches. Treat them as part of the project cost.
Can you give me a cost per hectolitre?
We would not trust one. Cost depends on scope, site and specification. Build the budget from quotes.
